summary: Cohort cold-start surge causing batch serialization, GPU credit bleed, and sustained dedicated throughput sag
summary_template: Incident: Dedicated pool throughput drop during cohort cold-start wave
description: Issue summary: Over a 90-minute window on 2026-03-10 morning (us-west peak), a cohort of newly-connected long-lived streams triggered a warmup-prefetch wave across multiple dedicated nodes. Symptoms were: elevated GPU attach latencies, serialized micro-batches (single-tenant serialization), unexpected GPU credit depletion for affected reserved pools, and a sustained ~35% p50 throughput loss for the customer's dedicated routes. Impact: Acme Analytics reported timeouts and elevated p99 latencies for inference endpoints that had been pinned to dedicated capacity. This affected production ML features (recommendations) with user-visible errors. Environment: prod - us-west dedicated pool serving redwood-open-13b variants. Observed behavior: - sudden spike in attach_time from ~40ms -> 800ms for many slots - batchers observed serializing previously-parallel short streams, increasing per-token CPU and GPU work - autoscaler attempted reactive scale-up but was throttled due to short-term GPU-credit constraints and allocation serialization - KV cache growth on a subset of connections caused memory pressure and longer prefetch times Expected behavior: normal cold-start/warmup should not cause neighbor-induced serialization or sustained GPU-credit bleed; autoscaler should maintain capacity SLOs and fall back to less aggressive prefetching when pool slot contention is detected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reserve a dedicated pool and pin redwood-open-13b (or quant variant)
2) Simulate 200 new long-lived streams connecting within a 2-3 minute window sending short prompts (10-50 tokens) repeatedly
3) Observe allocator attach_time and scheduler logs for slot serialization and prefetch events
4) Watch autoscaler decision timeline and GPU credit meters in the regional dashboard
observed_metrics_snapshot: p50 throughput -35% vs baseline; attach_time p95 from 60ms -> 1.2s; GPU slot utilization jumped from 70% -> 95%; GPU-credit-burn increased by 4x over 15 minutes; kv-cache entries per-connection rose ~12x for the offending cohort.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): customer routes pinned to pool-42 reported increased timeouts at 08:12 PDT; support validated with request traces and SDK logs.

SRE hypothesis: cohort coldstart wave created interleaved attach requests that our allocator serialized due to a conservative lock in the short-stream batcher; serialization led to longer per-attach windows and amplified GPU-credit consumption from repeated micro-prefetches.

Evidence: timeline correlation between connection fan-in (200 streams) and spike in kv_prefetch entries; attach latencies align with increased scheduler hold times; autoscaler backoff flagged due to GPU credit meter hitting reserve threshold.
Reproduced in staging by replaying connection pattern: observed identical attach-time and serialization pattern when connection fan-in rate > 60/s per node.

Potential root causes: allocator locking under short-stream churn; aggressive per-connection prefetch strategy that doesn't consider cohort-level fan-in; autoscaler gating by GPU-credit policy prevents immediate scale-up when repeated short attaches occur.
Related: linked to SUP-531020 behavior (miniwave fanout) and a recent autoscaler PR that enforces stricter GPU-credit safety margins.
comments: Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Customer reported elevated p99s and occasional 502s for dedicated endpoints; captured SDK traces and included request-ids. Slack thread: #support -> #incidents-dedicated-us-west.
SRE (Diego Marquez) 2026-03-10: Confirmed correlated attach_time spike and queue serialization in allocator logs; spinning up staging repro now.
Customer (Acme Oncall) 2026-03-10: Seeing partial recoveries when we reduce parallel streams; impacts critical morning traffic. Can you prioritize?

SRE (Diego Marquez) 2026-03-11: Temporary mitigations applied: lowered per-connection prefetch factor and bumped pool-42 GPU-credit ceiling to allow autoscaler to allocate immediately. Observed p50 throughput improved from -35% -> -12%.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted temporary workaround, requested ETA for permanent fix and prevention guidance for future cohort waves.
resolution_notes: Applied temporary mitigations at 2026-03-11T14:05Z: reduced per-connection prefetch multiplier from 4x -> 1.5x for pool-42, increased GPU-credit soft-cap by 25% to let autoscaler provision faster.
Result: attach_time p95 reduced to ~220ms within 10 minutes; p50 throughput recovered partially. No further customer-facing timeouts after mitigation.

Follow-up actions: 1) Bug filed against allocator lock path and short-stream batcher to allow lock-free attach ramping (GH PR referenced). 2) Autoscaler policy change proposal to treat repeated short attaches as a signal to preferentially scale capacity rather than gate on immediate GPU-credit thresholds. 3) Docs/Runbook update to include guidance for customers on onboarding large cohorts (stagger connections, warmup windows).
Permanent fix ETA: 2 sprints for allocator/batcher changes, 1 sprint for autoscaler policy updates; scheduling follow-up rollout with canary in us-east/us-west.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to prioritize allocator PR and associated unit/integration tests (owner: runtime-team)
2) Autoscaler owners to review GPU-credit gating logic and add cohort-detection heuristics (owner: autoscaler-team)
3) Schedule rollout with canary and monitor pool attach_time and GPU-credit burn metrics closely
4) Share runbook updates with Customer Success and include recommended warmup patterns for large cohort onboarding
